calibration.note: drawing is anisotropically stretched ~26x in y; all um values below are at the calibrated absolute scale (device coords: x in [0,120], y in [-2,+2], y_dev = 2 - y_image_um)

topology_reasoning.what_it_is: Symmetric superlattice-clad dual-core directional coupler. Two wide multimode slab cores (drawn width 0.471 um at calibrated scale, centered at y = +/-0.502) run parallel over the device length. They are coupled through a central lattice barrier of 5 thin parallel wires (w ~ 0.066, pitch ~ 0.1007) that spans the full 120 um. On the outer side of each core sits a 5-line periodic cladding (same ~0.100 pitch, w ~ 0.068) - a Bragg-like superlattice that mirrors the barrier so the two core modes stay index-balanced. Every feature in the cross-section sits on one uniform ~0.1-um lattice grid, which is the signature of a 1D-lattice (superlattice/SWG-type) coupler figure; the drawing exaggerates y ~26x, so the drawn 68-nm lines are the calibrated-scale rendering of the paper's subwavelength lattice.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: The two slab cores form a two-supermode system (even/odd). Power launched into one core beats between the cores with transfer length set by the supermode index split, which is engineered by the central 5-wire lattice barrier (pitch and fill factor set the barrier strength) and by the core-to-barrier gaps. The outer 5-line claddings terminate the field symmetrically on the outside of each core, keeping the two cores degenerate so complete power transfer is possible over the 120-um interaction length. Each core is fed from the chip edge: at all four corners a bent access band (the core's own end, swept up to the edge) plus the merged end of the 5-line cladding bundle exit the top/bottom edge as two parallel bands.
topology_reasoning.connectivity_measured: 10 connected components in the target: 5 independent full-length central wires; per half, (slab + both corner feed bands) is one piece reaching the chip edge, and (5 cladding lines merged at both bent ends into a second band) is another piece; plus one 46-px noise speck (ignored).
function_defining_knobs: coupling_length - straight interaction length of the slab cores (THE transfer-length knob; verified via verify_knob_response: delta_length 1:1 exact, area growth 4.69 vs 4.70 um^2 expected, passes=true)
slab_width / slab_y - core width and core-center offset (mode size; core-core separation)
center_pitch / center_y0 / n_center / center_widths - central lattice barrier period, position, wire count and fill (inter-core coupling strength)
clad_y_* / clad_w_* / n_clad - outer superlattice cladding geometry (mode balance)
FEED_PROFILE / BAND_PROFILE + segment widths - measured drawn centerlines of the corner access bends
